newsitem.title: USA: NYC debt service seen rising to 18 pct-state board.
newsitem.headline: NYC debt service seen rising to 18 pct-state board.

text.p: The New York State Financial Control Board, an important fiscal monitor of New York City, said on Tuesday that the city likely will continue to have difficulty balancing its budget.

The Board, in a statement released ahead of a report on the city's financial plan, also forecast that New York City's cost of debt service will rise to an average of 18 percent of tax revenues over the next four years, up from the 14-percent level achieved in the past four years.

The board highlighted another shift in the city's finances, noting that in the 1987 to 1996 fiscal period, both revenues and spending grew faster than inflation, while recurring revenues did not exceed recurring spending.

However, from fiscal 1997 to 2000, the board predicted that despite efforts by New York City to keep the rise in spending below the rate of inflation, revenues will rise even more slowly, worsening its structural imbalance.
"Unless recurring revenues and expenditures are brought into balance the city's difficulty in balancing each new budget will continue to increase," the Board said.

The monitor added any new public authority set up to sell city debt, an idea proposed by the Giuliani Administration, which is seeking to sidestep New York City's debt cap, must abide by strict rules. They include subjecting a new agency to the Financial Emergency Act and setting a comprehensive debt policy that requires pay-as-you-go financing for some capital spending and ensures assets are maintained.
